The method turns an intent of any size into working software. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to fill its Requirements from whatever the user has (a PRD, a brief, notes, a transcript), keep it in step with its sources, and slice from it.

A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed. ## Initiatives An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says. ## Start here - No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`. - Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`. - Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`. - Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. A PRD goes to John (`bmad-agent-pm`); a product brief, PRFAQ or BRD to Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`). - Has a piece of work and wants it better: - They have a draft in front of them (theirs or the model's) and want it pushed further, or want a critique method run on it → `bmad-advanced-elicitation`. It starts only by name: tell them to say "advanced elicitation", with the method if they have one in mind. - They ask for a review of a diff, a file, or a document → `bmad-review`. - They want several points of view arguing it out, a roundtable, or a focus group of their customers → `bmad-party-mode`. - Has large or raw input: - A transcript, a chat or email thread, a voice memo, or a long document they want what matters from (decisions, action items, key points) → `bmad-ingest`. - A document past about 50 KB that agents work from (an old spec, a vendor manual, a large PRD), or one already sharded that they want to change → `bmad-shard-pro`. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute. **The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. A transcript, a chat or email thread, or a voice memo goes through `bmad-ingest` first when it is installed, and the note it returns is the input. A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. The method adds note templates for `standup`, `retrospective` (the meeting, not `bmad-retrospective`'s epic review), `sprint-review`, `discovery-workshop` and `user-interview`. The four phases are analysis (ideation, research, is it worth building), planning (what exactly, and in what slices), implementation (build it), and validation (is it right). They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete. Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. # Meeting Room Booker

## Description

A single web page, run on the owner's computer, where office staff see which of the five meeting rooms are free today and book a free slot by giving their name, a meeting title and a length. The one rule that must never break is that bookings in a room do not overlap, even when two people book the same slot at once. It is a hobby project: the scope is the owner's stated idea (`_bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md`) and nothing more.

## Outcome

For office staff, finding and booking a free room for today takes one page and a few clicks, and no room is ever double-booked: shown by the Done when checks passing on the owner's computer.

## Requirements

- R1 (idea ¶1): One web page shows, for today, which rooms are free and which are booked, slot by slot.
- R2 (idea ¶2): The page lists exactly five rooms, Room 1–5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
- R3 (idea ¶3): Clicking a free slot lets a person book it with their name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours; the booking then shows as booked.
- R4 (idea ¶4): Two bookings in the same room never overlap; one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is allowed.
- R5 (idea ¶5): When two people book the same slot at the same moment, exactly one booking is stored and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."

## Constraints

- C1 (idea ¶6): Python with FastAPI and a SQLite database, running on the owner's own computer.
- C2 (idea ¶7, ¶8): Hobby scale; nothing is built for login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones or mobile.

## Done when

- Started on the owner's computer, the page shows Room 1–5 with their seat counts and today's free and booked slots.
- A booking made by clicking a free slot and filling in name, title and length shows as booked after a page reload.
- An automated test shows an overlapping booking in the same room is refused and a back-to-back one (ends 11:00, starts 11:00) is accepted.
- An automated test fires two simultaneous bookings for the same slot: exactly one is stored and the other gets "This slot has just been booked."

## Boundaries

- Out: login or accounts, repeat bookings, editing or cancelling a booking, time zones (all times are the computer's local time), mobile layout, hosting anywhere but the owner's computer.
- Tracer path: open the page → see today's grid of five rooms → click a free slot → submit name, title and length → booking stored in SQLite → grid shows the slot booked.

## References

- source — _bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md, ¶1–¶8

## Notes

- Decision (2026-11-12): The bookable day is 08:00–18:00 in the computer's local time, and a booking must end by 18:00.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Slots start on the half hour, and lengths are 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Only today can be viewed and booked, and slots already past cannot be booked.
- Decision (2026-11-12): The five rooms are fixed seed data, with no screen to add or edit them.
- Decision (2026-11-12): A booked slot shows the booker's name and meeting title to everyone; with no login it is the only way to know whose meeting it is.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No epics; the initiative is split straight into three or four small stories in `tickets/tickets.toml`, at the owner's request.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Tracer bullet is story 1, a 30-minute booking end to end through page, API and SQLite; story 2, overlap and same-moment bookings, follows as the least certain part.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No closing "Refactor sweep" story; the owner asked for three or four stories. Add one later if deferred cleanup builds up.

- `<folder>` is an epic folder name, `backlog`, or the initiative, by default the active one, where `next` and `status` add a `backlog` key to show. On a parent initiative they list its child initiatives under `initiatives`.
- With a tracker, sync first (Tracker sync) and pass `--synced` to `next`.

Act with the user on any non-empty key:

- `unpinned_after`: add the epic's `after` prerequisite to the entry that needs it.
- `undeclared_after`: add the awaited epic, with its `needs`, to its epic's `after` in the breakdown, or drop the prerequisite.
- `order_conflict`: reorder or merge the epics, or record why in a `Decision:` line.
- `drift`: make the leaf file's and the entry's `after` or `hitl` equal.
- `problems`: an orphan plan gets its `ticket` set to the entry id or file stem; an unknown status is fixed with `mark`.
- `waiting_on` on a `blocked` row: say what the ticket waits on.
- `unknown` on a `blocked` row: settle it, remove it, and add a dated `Decision:` line to the file's Notes, or its epic's when it has no file.

## Publish

On the repo store, approval commits (Conventions in `workflow.md`) and `publication` does not apply. On a tracker, publication is `at_inception`: `at_inception` offers to publish the agreed set after validation; `on_start` publishes each ticket when it starts. An explicit user request overrides it.

Publish to a tracker through `write`:

- Write the leaf's file first (`tickets.py pull` if none); send it minus the frontmatter lines `tracker_id`, `remote`, `tracker_status`, `status`, and `assignee`.
- Create parents and prerequisites first, adding local prerequisites to the scope. An `after` naming a sibling's id or `<epic id>.<entry id>` is that entry's remote item; `epic-<slug>` is the epic's.
- A type mapped to `""` is never sent; its children attach to the nearest published ancestor. Say so once.
- Offer `setup` at first publish, or when the tracker lacks something the maps or `fields` name.
- Then mirror, and edit a published container's `tracker_id` and `remote` into its file.

An unrefined ticket may be published with `refined: false`; refinement updates the same file and remote item.

## Start

Offer the first `ready_to_start` row of `next` in build order, or every unassigned one when work can run in parallel. `find` it with the row's `ref`, refine a `ready_to_refine` one first per `ticket.md`, and confirm it is unassigned; the builder reads the ticket. With the user's approval, start it: on a tracker, publish it if needed, `write` it to `[tickets.status].in-progress` and mirror; on the repo store, write nothing. Then hand it to `bmad-build` or `bmad-build-auto`.

Only an unattended run's orchestrator honors the row's `plan_checkpoint` and `done_checkpoint`.

## Status

The plan is `<type>-<slug>-plan.md` beside where the leaf's file is or would be, linked by its `ticket`; the leaf file's `status` counts only without a plan.

- **A container's** `status` is Sofia's to edit in its file: absent until its first ticket starts, then `in-progress`, then `done` or `dropped` on the user's confirmation; a published one transitions through `write`.

- A failed store call: tell the user what blocks it, confirm the setup, and ask them to authenticate if that is the cause. An empty verb field you cannot infer: ask, and offer to record it per `store-setup.md`.

# Meeting Room Booker

## Description

A single web page, run on the owner's computer, where office staff see which of the five meeting rooms are free today and book a free slot by giving their name, a meeting title and a length. The one rule that must never break is that bookings in a room do not overlap, even when two people book the same slot at once. It is a hobby project: the scope is the owner's stated idea (`_bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md`) and nothing more.

## Outcome

For office staff, finding and booking a free room for today takes one page and a few clicks, and no room is ever double-booked: shown by the Done when checks passing on the owner's computer.

## Requirements

- R1 (idea ¶1): One web page shows, for today, which rooms are free and which are booked, slot by slot.
- R2 (idea ¶2): The page lists exactly five rooms, Room 1–5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
- R3 (idea ¶3): Clicking a free slot lets a person book it with their name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours; the booking then shows as booked.
- R4 (idea ¶4): Two bookings in the same room never overlap; one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is allowed.
- R5 (idea ¶5): When two people book the same slot at the same moment, exactly one booking is stored and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."

## Constraints

- C1 (idea ¶6): Python with FastAPI and a SQLite database, running on the owner's own computer.
- C2 (idea ¶7, ¶8): Hobby scale; nothing is built for login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones or mobile.

## Done when

- Started on the owner's computer, the page shows Room 1–5 with their seat counts and today's free and booked slots.
- A booking made by clicking a free slot and filling in name, title and length shows as booked after a page reload.
- An automated test shows an overlapping booking in the same room is refused and a back-to-back one (ends 11:00, starts 11:00) is accepted.
- An automated test fires two simultaneous bookings for the same slot: exactly one is stored and the other gets "This slot has just been booked."

## Boundaries

- Out: login or accounts, repeat bookings, editing or cancelling a booking, time zones (all times are the computer's local time), mobile layout, hosting anywhere but the owner's computer.
- Tracer path: open the page → see today's grid of five rooms → click a free slot → submit name, title and length → booking stored in SQLite → grid shows the slot booked.

## References

- source — _bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md, ¶1–¶8

## Notes

- Decision (2026-11-12): The bookable day is 08:00–18:00 in the computer's local time, and a booking must end by 18:00.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Slots start on the half hour, and lengths are 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Only today can be viewed and booked, and slots already past cannot be booked.
- Decision (2026-11-12): The five rooms are fixed seed data, with no screen to add or edit them.
- Decision (2026-11-12): A booked slot shows the booker's name and meeting title to everyone; with no login it is the only way to know whose meeting it is.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No epics; the initiative is split straight into three or four small stories in `tickets/tickets.toml`, at the owner's request.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Tracer bullet is story 1, a 30-minute booking end to end through page, API and SQLite; story 2, overlap and same-moment bookings, follows as the least certain part.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No closing "Refactor sweep" story; the owner asked for three or four stories. Add one later if deferred cleanup builds up.
